clue.text: Boy I imprisoned in vault with no locks

indicators.note: a prisoner is shut inside, so the letter is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: an arch is a vaulted structure
someone with no locks of hair is bald

explanation.surface: A boy is locked up in a vault, and he has no hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text dropped the I printed after 'Boy'; the page shows it. 'with no locks' means hairless, not unbolted.
explanation.definitionFit: Archibald is a traditional male given name, so it fits a boy.

clue.text: Fun post being dropped off by 2 cars?

definitions.text: Fun post being dropped off by 2 cars?

parts.words: Fun post being dropped off by 2 cars?
parts.note: the merriment that follows (post) a day skiing, once cable cars have taken you down

explanation.surface: Enjoyment after leaving a mail delivery from cable cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer to 2 down, so '2 cars' are cable cars; 'post' is Latin and French for after.
explanation.definitionFit: Apres-ski is the socialising that follows a day on the slopes.

clue.text: Lead around island, travelling north

parts.note: c, short for circa, means around

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A leash round an island, heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is an electric flex or wire, so a cable.

clue.text: Case bringing with it team work

parts.note: to be in is to be fashionable, with it
a side is a sports team
a job is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A suitcase brings along a team's labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is a criminal case; 'bringing' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a crime committed with help from someone within, so a particular kind of case.

clue.text: "Reformed" characters hack into a computer resource

indicators.note: going inside, so the horse goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: RAM is a computer's random-access memory
a hack is a worn-out horse, a nag

explanation.surface: Someone changed hacks their way into a computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like computer intrusion; it is an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram is a word whose letters have been rearranged, or reformed.

clue.text: Battles over flat of French bachelor involved in rent rise

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: caught up within, so the bachelor goes inside
torn apart, so the letters of rise are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disputes about a French bachelor's flat when the rent goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent rise' looks like a rent increase; 'rent' means torn, rearranging RISE into RIES, and 'involved in' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is a famous flat horse race, and derbies are contests run on the flat.

clue.text: Racket in Cornwall, perhaps, is heard by all

parts.note: Cornwall is a county in the South West of England, SW, given as an example

indicators.note: what everyone hears, the spoken sound, is meant rather than the spelling

parts.note: said aloud, the word is rhymes with fizz

explanation.surface: Some swindle down in Cornwall is common knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England, so 'perhaps' marks it as one example of SW.
explanation.definitionFit: A swizz is British slang for a swindle, and a racket is a scam.

clue.text: Chance to express one's displeasure

definitions.meaning: a slight chance, as in not getting a whiff of success
to draw breath sharply through the nose in disdain

explanation.definitionFit: A sniff is a slim chance, and to sniff is to show disdain.

clue.text: One donation finally is going to hospital, God willing

annotationWithheld.why: One donation finally is going to hospital, God willing: I + N + SHALL + H leaves the A of INSHALLAH unsourced; the clue as held seems to lack a word (perhaps 'a'), not visible on the scan
annotationWithheld.clue: One donation finally is going to hospital, God willing

clue.text: Miner's enthusiasm for short time that's rubbing off on Clementine

indicators.note: standing in place of, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: the word miner, with the 's as a link
min is the short form of minute
zest is enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Clementine, the miner's daughter of the song, catches enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: ZEST replaces MIN in MINER. The song's Clementine is a miner's daughter, but the definition means the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A zester is a kitchen tool that scrapes the peel off citrus fruit like clementines.

clue.text: Puzzle about payment returned

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for payment is written backwards

parts.note: a sub is a subscription payment

explanation.surface: A puzzle over a payment that came back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle, one specific kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Simulated greetings from fools circling annoy one

indicators.note: going round, so the fools' letters surround the other pieces

parts.note: asses are fools
to irk is to annoy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Idiots surround someone with fake kisses that irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Air kisses are pretend kisses blown near the cheek, greetings that are simulated rather than real.

clue.text: Faint right after seizing receiver? The exact opposite!

indicators.note: taking hold of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the exclamation tells us to take opposites: the opposite of a receiver is a sender
taking the opposite again, right becomes left, abbreviated L

explanation.surface: Someone weak-kneed grabs a telephone handset, or does the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the wordplay puts R next to a receiver; 'The exact opposite!' flips every element, so L (left) is held by SENDER instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slight or small, as in a slender or faint chance.

clue.text: I call to embrace gutted football fan

indicators.note: to hug, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: with insides removed, leaving only the first and last letters of football

explanation.surface: A supporter is called upon to hug a disappointed football follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' looks like a supporter, but it is the verb, as in fanning flames.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan a fire or feelings is to stoke them, the verb sense of making them burn hotter.

clue.text: British Library in Beijing makes new version of books

indicators.note: a new form of these letters is wanted, so they are rearranged

parts.note: BL is the standard abbreviation for the British Library

explanation.surface: A Chinese library produces a fresh edition of some volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: The King James Bible is the 1611 English translation, one version of the biblical books.

clue.text: Pioneer gel intended to bring colour back

indicators.note: backwards, so the found letters are read in reverse
these words bring along the letters inside them, running across the words

explanation.surface: A pioneering gel was meant to restore colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile green is a pale bluish-green shade, a named colour.

clue.text: Girl's lifted dripping, clutching hot dish

indicators.note: holding tight, so the hot letter goes inside

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name, plus S from the possessive
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: raised up in a down clue, so the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: dripping means wet

explanation.surface: A girl raises a dripping hot dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'lifted' means read upwards, so backwards; 'clutching' puts the hot letter inside, right after the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a mutton and potato stew, a well-known dish.

clue.text: Attacked and wounded dies, alas

indicators.note: hurt or damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A victim is assaulted and injured and, sadly, dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Assailed is a synonym of attacked.

clue.text: Staff's consuming port and energy snacks

indicators.note: eating up, so the staff's letters surround the rest

parts.note: a club is a staff, plus the S from the possessive
Sandwich is an old port in Kent
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Workers drink port and gobble energy bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent, south-east England, one of the historic Cinque Ports.
explanation.definitionFit: Club sandwiches are triple-decker filled sandwiches, a type of snack.

clue.text: Ernie is one a friend married

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: Ernie is someone that a pal married.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that picks the UK's Premium Bond winners: Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: ERNIE is formed from initial letters, which makes it an example of that kind of word.

clue.text: Dark pit in hell's obscuring one

indicators.note: placed within, so the pit goes inside hell's letters

parts.note: Dis is the underworld, hell; plus the possessive S

indicators.note: hiding, so the letter for one is taken out of view

parts.note: a mine is a pit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dark pit in the underworld hides someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscuring one' removes I from MINE, leaving MNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimness means darkness or lack of light, the noun sense of the dark.

clue.text: Lying about our party being exploited

indicators.note: around, so the bed-ridden word surrounds the party

parts.note: abed means lying in bed
our side is us

explanation.surface: Lies about our political party being taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths, but it is lying down, ABED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abused is to be ill-treated or taken unfair advantage of, so exploited.

clue.text: Outsize mop's one I grab roughly, squeezing hard

indicators.note: holding tight, so the hard letter goes inside the rearranged letters
done roughly, the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a big mop roughly with a firm grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' turns I I GRAB into BIGAIR, and 'squeezing' puts H inside it; the 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: Big hair is a large, teased, voluminous hairstyle, an example of an outsize mop of hair.

clue.text: March girl round icy track, initially to generate warmth

indicators.note: surrounding, so the girl's name goes around the other letters

parts.note: Amy March is one of the sisters in Little Women

indicators.note: the opening letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A girl in March goes round an icy track to warm up.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendliness, warmth of feeling between people.

clue.text: Sage stuffing mother's pork pie?

indicators.note: filling, so the hat goes inside the word for mother

parts.note: mama is mother; the 's means has, as the mother holds the stuffing
a pork pie is a type of hat with a flat crown

explanation.surface: A wise man is filling his mother's pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' looks like food; it is the flat-topped hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title for a revered wise person, so a sage.

clue.text: One may be alarmed and more scared with loss of identity

indicators.note: losing, so the letters for identity are removed

parts.note: timider means more scared or more fearful
ID is the abbreviation for identity

explanation.surface: Someone frightened, more scared still, loses their identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarmed' means fitted with an alarm, not frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen timer can be set with an alarm to ring at the end.

clue.text: It may stand in North East, outside English town

parts.note: stet is a proofreading mark meaning let it stand

indicators.note: placed around, so the first pieces surround the English letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something might stand in the North East, beyond an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Etienne is an industrial town in south-east France.

clue.text: Tongue that would wag heartlessly?

parts.note: a language whose name, losing its central letter, becomes the part of a dog that wags

explanation.surface: A gossip's tongue wagging without feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a language spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka, and tongue means language.

clue.text: Marathon running strips one of stylish ways

definitions.meaning: a long-running comic, whose strips ran from 1937 to 2012
a man of fashionable habits, a fop

explanation.surface: A long race leaves someone stylish with stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy was a long-running British children's comic; 'strips' means comic strips, not undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man devoted to stylish dress, and the Dandy was a comic of very long run.

clue.text: Global competition's fairest

parts.note: the winner of a worldwide beauty pageant, reading fairest as most beautiful rather than most just

explanation.definitionFit: The title goes to the winner of the international beauty contest, judged the most beautiful.
